examples.ko: 동네 교습소에서 피아노 교습을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: I am taking piano lessons at a local studio.
The lesson was so long that it was tiring.

examples.ko: 수영 교습은 한 달에 몇 번 있어요?
examples.en: How many times a month are the swimming lessons?
The lesson fee is a bit expensive, so I am worried.

examples.ko: 개인 교습으로 영어를 배우니까 빨리 늘어요.
examples.en: Learning English through private lessons improves it quickly.
I signed up for driving lessons during the vacation.

explain: 학원이나 교습소에서 기술을 배우는 느낌이 강하고, '교습소', '교습비', '개인 교습'처럼 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '레슨'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It has a strong feel of learning a skill at an academy or studio, and is common in words like '교습소', '교습비' and '개인 교습'. In daily talk people also often say '레슨'.

en: have a meeting or one-on-one talk with

examples.en: I have a meeting with my homeroom teacher tomorrow.
The team leader met the new employees one by one.
We set a time to meet with the parents.
I was very nervous during the meeting.
After talking with my professor, I decided on my career path.
I met the boss in the afternoon and explained the situation.

explain: 상담은 고민을 말하고 조언을 받는 것에 가깝고, 면담은 약속을 잡고 만나서 이야기하는 것에 가까워요. 선생님이나 상사처럼 윗사람과 만날 때 많이 쓰고, '면담을 신청하다', '면담을 하다'로 같이 써요.
explain_en: 상담 is closer to sharing a worry and getting advice; 면담 is meeting someone by appointment to talk. It is often used with a teacher or boss, as in '면담을 신청하다' (request a meeting) and '면담을 하다'.

en: book or cast (a guest, speaker, performer, or location); contact and line up

examples.en: The broadcaster booked a famous singer.
I am busy lining up a lecturer for the event.

examples.ko: 촬영 장소를 섭외하는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Securing a filming location is not easy.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리가 연사를 섭외해서 강연회를 열었어요.
examples.en: Our club lined up a speaker and held a lecture.

examples.ko: 그 배우를 섭외하려고 몇 달 동안 연락했어요.
examples.en: We kept contacting that actor for months to book them.

examples.ko: 사회자를 섭외할 때 비용도 같이 이야기해요.
examples.en: When we book a host, we discuss the fee as well.

explain: 출연할 사람이나 촬영할 장소를 알아보고 연락해서 와 달라고 부탁하는 일이에요. 방송, 행사, 촬영에서 자주 써요. '섭외가 들어오다', '섭외가 되다'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. '초대하다'는 손님으로 부르는 것이고, 섭외하다는 일을 맡기려고 교섭하는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: It means finding a performer or a location, contacting them, and asking them to take part. It is common in broadcasting, events, and filming, and also as a noun in '섭외가 들어오다' and '섭외가 되다'. '초대하다' is inviting someone as a guest, while 섭외하다 is negotiating to have them do a job.

examples.en: The computer lab is on the third floor.
After class I practiced in the practice room.

examples.ko: 실습실이 밤 열 시까지 열려 있어요.
examples.en: The practice room is open until ten at night.
You have to wear gloves in the chemistry lab.
A new practice room opened, and students like it.
You must apply in advance to use the practice room.

explain: '교실'은 앉아서 듣는 수업을 하는 곳이고 '실습실'은 직접 손으로 해 보는 수업을 하는 곳이에요. '컴퓨터 실습실', '요리 실습실'처럼 앞에 과목을 붙여요. 과학 실험을 하는 방은 '실험실'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A '교실' is for sitting and listening; a '실습실' is for hands-on classes. Put the subject in front: '컴퓨터 실습실', '요리 실습실'. A room for science experiments is a '실험실'.

examples.en: If an agent comes in your place, a letter of attorney is a must.
The bank told me to submit a letter of attorney.

examples.ko: 위임장에 도장을 찍고 신분증 사본도 붙였어요.
examples.en: I stamped the letter of attorney and attached a copy of my ID too.

examples.ko: 위임장은 개인이 작성하는 사문서라서 도장이나 서명이 필요해요.
examples.en: A letter of attorney is a private document written by an individual, so it needs a seal or signature.

examples.ko: 위임장 없이는 서류를 받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't pick up the documents without a letter of attorney.
I got a letter of attorney form from the community center.

explain: 본인이 직접 못 할 때 다른 사람에게 일을 맡긴다는 내용을 적는 서류예요. 보통 '위임장을 쓰다/내다/제출하다'로 말하고, 은행·주민센터·회사에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the document you write when you cannot do something yourself and let someone else do it for you. People usually say '위임장을 쓰다/내다/제출하다', and it often comes up at banks, community centers and companies.

en: commission; request (a professional to do a job)

examples.en: The company commissioned a designer to make a new logo.

examples.ko: 이 일은 전문가에게 의뢰하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is better to hand this job to an expert.
I called the hospital to request a test.
I am looking for a place to order a translation.

examples.ko: 친구가 저에게 그림을 의뢰해서 열심히 그렸어요.
examples.en: A friend commissioned a painting from me, so I worked hard on it.

examples.ko: 수리를 의뢰하고 나서 사흘 뒤에 받았어요.
examples.en: I got it back three days after I requested the repair.

explain: 전문가나 전문 기관에 일을 맡길 때 써요. '부탁하다'는 가까운 사이에도 쓰지만 '의뢰하다'는 번역, 수리, 검사처럼 업무를 맡기는 느낌이에요. 명사 '의뢰'로 '의뢰가 들어오다'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you hand a job to a professional or a specialized organization. '부탁하다' works between close people, but '의뢰하다' feels like handing over work such as translation, repairs or tests. The noun '의뢰' appears in phrases like '의뢰가 들어오다' (a request comes in).

examples.ko: 하루 종일 잡무에 시달려서 정작 중요한 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was bogged down in odd jobs all day and couldn't do the really important work.
New employees first learn the miscellaneous tasks.
There were so many chores that I worked overtime.

examples.ko: 서류 정리 같은 잡무는 제가 맡을게요.
examples.en: I'll take care of odd jobs like organizing documents.

examples.ko: 이 일 말고도 잡무를 여러 개 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: Besides this job, I'm handling several other small tasks.
I couldn't even eat lunch because I was dealing with odd jobs.

explain: 맡은 주요 일이 아닌 자질구레한 일을 말해요. 주로 회사나 학교 같은 사무 환경에서 쓰고, '잡무가 많다/밀리다'처럼 말해요. 집이나 현장의 허드렛일까지 넓게 말할 때는 '잡일'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means small miscellaneous tasks that are not your main duties. It is used mostly in offices and schools, as in '잡무가 많다/밀리다'. For general odd jobs around the house or a work site, '잡일' is used more.

examples.ko: 재확인 결과 서류에는 아무 문제가 없었어요.
examples.en: After double-checking, there was no problem with the documents.

examples.ko: 이름과 연락처는 재확인이 꼭 필요한 항목이에요.
examples.en: Your name and contact info are items that definitely need to be double-checked.

examples.ko: 출발하기 전에 비행기 시간을 한 번 더 재확인했어요.
examples.en: Before leaving, I double-checked the flight time once more.
Please call and double-check that the reservation is right.
The teacher told us to double-check the exam date.

examples.ko: 이 대회로 제 실력을 재확인할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: This competition let me confirm my skills once again.

explain: 이미 한 번 확인한 약속, 예약, 숫자를 다시 확인할 때 써요. 실력이나 마음처럼 이미 알던 것을 다시 분명히 알게 됐을 때도 말해요. '다시 확인하다', '한 번 더 확인하다'로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when you check again something you already checked, like an appointment, reservation or number. It also works when you become sure again of something you already knew, like your skills or feelings. People also often say '다시 확인하다' or '한 번 더 확인하다'.

examples.en: I work as the teacher's assistant.
The assistant organized the documents for me.
I sat in the passenger seat and gave directions.
They say the lab is hiring a new assistant.

examples.ko: 조수의 도움 덕분에 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the assistant's help, the work finished quickly.
The chef's assistant prepares the ingredients.

explain: 조수는 전문가 곁에서 일을 돕는 사람이라 연구실·병원·주방처럼 기술을 가진 사람 밑에서 일하는 경우가 많아요. 자동차 앞자리 오른쪽은 '조수석'이라고 불러요. 같은 소리의 '조수'는 바닷물이 들고 나는 것도 뜻해서 글의 맥락으로 구분해요.
explain_en: A 조수 helps a skilled person, so it is common in labs, clinics, and kitchens. The front passenger seat of a car is called '조수석'. The same-sounding '조수' also means the tide, so context tells them apart.

en: arrange; set up (a meeting, a job)

examples.en: My friend set up a blind date for me.
My teacher arranged the interview.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 만남을 주선하는 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need someone to set up a meeting between the two companies.

examples.ko: 제가 모임을 주선할 테니 날짜만 알려 주세요.
examples.en: I'll organize the gathering, so just tell me the date.

examples.ko: 삼촌이 일자리를 주선해서 다음 주부터 일해요.
examples.en: My uncle found me a job, so I start next week.
The person who arranged the meeting is the team leader.

explain: 소개팅, 면접, 일자리처럼 사람을 연결해 주는 자리를 만들 때 써요. '소개하다'는 사람을 알려 주는 것이고, '주선하다'는 만남이나 일이 이루어지도록 애써 주는 것까지 들어가요.
explain_en: It is used when making an occasion that connects people, such as a blind date, interview or job. '소개하다' is introducing someone, while '주선하다' also includes making the effort so that the meeting or job actually happens.

examples.en: Please gather the documents in order and bind them.

examples.ko: 영수증은 한 장씩 풀로 붙이지 말고 철하세요.
examples.en: Don't glue receipts one by one; file them together.
If you staple the pages together, they're easy to turn.

examples.ko: 이 노트는 실로 철해서 만든 거예요.
examples.en: This notebook was made by binding the pages with thread.

examples.ko: 서류를 철한 파일을 책상 위에 올려 뒀어요.
examples.en: I left the file with the bound documents on the desk.
Before binding the contract, I checked the date first.

explain: 종이를 모아서 스테이플러, 끈, 실 등으로 한데 묶어 두는 일에 써요. '묶다'보다 서류나 종이 묶음에 더 잘 맞아요. 이렇게 묶은 것을 '서류철'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for gathering papers and fastening them together with a stapler, string or thread. It fits documents and paper bundles better than '묶다' (to tie). The bundle itself is also called '서류철'.
